question.text:
Consider the following polynomial division:

\begin{align*} \require{enclose} & \phantom{-x-3} \:\:\:\:\:\:\:\: 6x^2 -13x - 5 \\ & -x+2 \: \enclose{longdiv}{ -6x^3 +25x^2 -21x + 10 \:\:} \\ & \phantom{-x-3} \:\:\:\:\: \underline{-6x^3+12x^2} \\ & \phantom{-x-3} \:\:\:\:\:\:\: \phantom{-6x^3+} 13x^2-21x+10 \\ & \phantom{-x-3} \:\:\:\:\:\:\: \phantom{-6x^3+} \underline{13x^2-26x} \\ & \phantom{-x-3} \:\:\:\:\:\:\: \phantom{-6x^3+13x^2-} \phantom{2}5x +10 \\ & \phantom{-x-3} \:\:\:\:\:\:\: \phantom{-6x^3+13x^2+} \underline{\phantom{2}5x-10} \\ & \phantom{-x-3} \:\:\:\:\:\:\: \phantom{-6x^3+13x^2+25x -} 20 \\ \end{align*}

From the above, $\dfrac{-6x^3 + 25x^2 -21x + 10}{-x+2}=$
question.explanation:
\begin{align*} \require{enclose} & \phantom{-x-3} \:\:\:\:\:\:\:\: {\color{blue}6x^2 -13x - 5} \\ & {\color{purple}-x+2} \: \enclose{longdiv}{\:\, -6x^3 +25x^2 -21x + 10 \:\:} \\ & \phantom{-x-3} \:\:\:\:\: \underline{-6x^3+12x^2} \\ & \phantom{-x-3} \:\:\:\:\:\:\: \phantom{-6x^3+} 13x^2-21x+10 \\ & \phantom{-x-3} \:\:\:\:\:\:\: \phantom{-6x^3+} \underline{13x^2-26x} \\ & \phantom{-x-3} \:\:\:\:\:\:\: \phantom{-6x^3+13x^2-} \phantom{2}5x +10 \\ & \phantom{-x-3} \:\:\:\:\:\:\: \phantom{-6x^3+13x^2+} \underline{\phantom{2}5x-10} \\ & \phantom{-x-3} \:\:\:\:\:\:\: \phantom{-6x^3+13x^2+25x -} {\color{red}20} \\ \end{align*}

From the given polynomial division, we deduce that dividing the polynomial $-6x^3 + 25x^2 -21x + 10$ by the linear binomial ${\color{purple}-x+2}$ gives

  • the quotient ${\color{blue}6x^2 -13x -5},$ and

  • the remainder ${\color{red}20}.$

Therefore, we obtain

\[ \dfrac{-6x^3 + 25x^2 -21x + 10}{-x+2}={\color{blue} 6x^2 -13x - 5 }+\dfrac{\color{red}20}{\color{purple}-x+2}. \]

question.text:
Consider the following polynomial division:

\begin{align*} \require{enclose} & \phantom{x+2} \:\:\:\:\: x^2 +4x + 3 \\ & x+2 \: \enclose{longdiv}{\:\, x^3 +6x^2 +11x + 11 \:\:} \\ & \phantom{x-3} \:\:\:\:\: \underline{x^3+2x^2} \\ & \phantom{x-3} \:\:\:\:\:\:\: \phantom{x^3+} 4x^2+11x+11 \\ & \phantom{x-3} \:\:\:\:\:\:\: \phantom{x^3+} \underline{4x^2+\phantom{1}8x} \\ & \phantom{x-3} \:\:\:\:\:\:\: \phantom{x^3+4x^2+} \phantom{1}3x + 11 \\ & \phantom{x-3} \:\:\:\:\:\:\: \phantom{x^3+4x^2+} \underline{\phantom{1}3x+\phantom{1}6} \\ & \phantom{x-3} \:\:\:\:\:\:\: \phantom{x^3+4x^2+11x+} \phantom{1}5 \\ \end{align*}

From the above, $\dfrac{x^3 +6x^2 +11x + 11}{x+2}=$
question.explanation:
\begin{align*} \require{enclose} & \phantom{x+2} \:\:\:\:\: {\color{blue}x^2 +4x + 3} \\ & {\color{purple}x+2} \: \enclose{longdiv}{\:\, x^3 +6x^2 +11x + 11 \:\:} \\ & \phantom{x-3} \:\:\:\:\: \underline{x^3+2x^2} \\ & \phantom{x-3} \:\:\:\:\:\:\: \phantom{x^3+} 4x^2+11x+11 \\ & \phantom{x-3} \:\:\:\:\:\:\: \phantom{x^3+} \underline{4x^2+\phantom{1}8x} \\ & \phantom{x-3} \:\:\:\:\:\:\: \phantom{x^3+4x^2+} \phantom{1}3x + 11 \\ & \phantom{x-3} \:\:\:\:\:\:\: \phantom{x^3+4x^2+} \underline{\phantom{1}3x+\phantom{1}6} \\ & \phantom{x-3} \:\:\:\:\:\:\: \phantom{x^3+4x^2+11x+} {\color{red}\phantom{1}5} \\ \end{align*}

From the given polynomial division, we deduce that dividing the polynomial $x^3 +6x^2 +11x + 11$ by the linear binomial ${\color{purple}x+2}$ gives

  • the quotient ${\color{blue}x^2 +4x + 3},$ and

  • the remainder ${\color{red}5}.$

Therefore, we obtain

\[ \dfrac{x^3 +6x^2 +11x + 11}{x+2}={\color{blue} x^2 +4x + 3 }+\dfrac{\color{red}5}{\color{purple}x+2}. \]

exampleAnswers.title: Dividing a Polynomial With Some Zero Coefficients by a Linear Binomial

question.text:
From top to bottom, what are the missing expressions in the following polynomial division problem?

\begin{align*} \require{enclose} & \phantom{x-1} \:\:\:\: \fbox{$\phantom{6x +6}$} \\ & x-1 \: \enclose{longdiv}{\:\, 6x^2 +0x - 1} \\ & \phantom{x-1} \:\:\:\:\: \underline{6x^2-6x} \\ & \phantom{x-1} \:\:\:\:\: \phantom{6x^2-\:} 6x-1 \\ & \phantom{x-1} \:\:\:\:\:\: \phantom{6x^2-} \underline{\fbox{$\phantom{6x-6}$}} \\ & \phantom{x-1} \:\:\:\:\:\: \phantom{6x^2-6x-\:} \! 5 \\ \end{align*}
question.explanation:
Notice that the dividend is missing the $x$-term. So, we write it using a zero coefficient, as follows:

\[ 6x^2 + {\color{red}0}x - 1 \]

Using the method of polynomial division, we obtain the following:

\begin{align*} \require{enclose} & \phantom{x-1} \:\:\:\:\: {\color{blue}6x +6} \\ & x-1 \: \enclose{longdiv}{\:\, 6x^2 +0x - 1} \\ & \phantom{x-1} \:\:\:\:\: \underline{6x^2-6x} \\ & \phantom{x-1} \:\:\:\:\: \phantom{6x^2-\:} 6x-1 \\ & \phantom{x-1} \:\:\:\:\:\:\: \phantom{6x^2-} \underline{\color{blue}6x-6} \\ & \phantom{x-1} \:\:\:\:\:\: \phantom{6x^2-6x-\:} \! 5 \\ \end{align*}

Therefore, the missing expressions are

$\qquad$ $6x+6\quad$ and $\quad 6x-6.$

example.title: Dividing a Polynomial With Some Zero Coefficients by a Linear Binomial

question.text:
From top to bottom, what are the missing expressions in the following polynomial division problem?

\begin{align*} \require{enclose} & \phantom{x+2} \:\:\:\: \fbox{$\phantom{x -2}$} \\ & x+2 \: \enclose{longdiv}{\:\, x^2 +0x - 9} \\ & \phantom{x+2} \:\:\:\:\: \underline{x^2+2x} \\ & \phantom{x+2} \:\:\:\:\: \phantom{x^2} -2x-9 \\ & \phantom{x+2} \:\:\:\:\:\: \phantom{x^2} \underline{\fbox{$\phantom{-\:2x-4}$}} \\ & \phantom{x+2} \:\:\:\:\:\: \phantom{x^2-2x} \! -5 \\ \end{align*}
question.explanation:
Notice that the dividend is missing the $x$-term. So, we write it using a zero coefficient, as follows:

\[ x^2 + {\color{red}0}x - 9 \]

Using the method of polynomial division, we obtain the following:

\begin{align*} \require{enclose} & \phantom{x+2} \:\:\:\:\: {\color{blue}x -2} \\ & x+2 \: \enclose{longdiv}{\:\, x^2 +0x - 9} \\ & \phantom{x+2} \:\:\:\:\: \underline{x^2+2x} \\ & \phantom{x+2} \:\:\:\:\: \phantom{x^2} -2x-9 \\ & \phantom{x+2} \:\:\:\:\:\: \phantom{x^2} \underline{\color{blue}-\:2x-4} \\ & \phantom{x+2} \:\:\:\:\:\: \phantom{x^2-2x} \! -5 \\ \end{align*}

Therefore, the missing expressions are

$\qquad$ $x-2\quad$ and $\quad -2x-4.$
